headline: Transcriptomic profiling nominates candidate genes and ML signatures in tumor and disease
label: Transcriptomic Biomarker Candidate Prioritization
summary: Recent studies combine public cohorts, single-cell RNA-seq and machine learning to prioritize transcriptomic biomarkers in disease microenvironments.
synthesis: The common thread is transcriptomic biomarker prioritization on public and multi-omic cohorts, with candidate genes carried into prognostic or diagnostic models. Several items localize candidates to specific cell states: the GPRC5A+ epithelial subset in colorectal cancer, the ANGPTL4+ macrophage subpopulation in aortic dissection, and an L1CAM-positive fibroblast-associated stromal state linked to reduced T/NK cytotoxicity features. Machine-learning gene selection yields a three-gene EMT signature in prostate cancer, a seven-gene MDRGG diagnostic model with AUC above 0.85 in validation, and an eight-gene CMS4 model informed by promoter methylation. Validation is heterogeneous; the diabetic retinopathy and Parkinson's analysis nominates A2M, NRP1, ETS2 and a predicted ITGB2-ICAM1 interaction as exploratory candidates. What is new is the consistent layering of single-cell state, stromal or immune context, and ML-based selection onto bulk cohorts, rather than a shared mechanism.
